# s217 — Merge independent item fields without guessing list or queue edits

Run branches and main can change independent items or different fields of an existing item. Extend the existing planned driver to preserve both changes, while leaving genuine disagreements explicit.

**Findings:** agents feedback 2026-10-05 U8; docs/feedback/agents-2026-10-05.md · **Size:** L · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-06** — Ready for review: the slicer-index driver (src/slicer/mergeindex.py) merges index.json by identity. Items match by id and object fields by name; lists, prose and passes are atomic; next_id stays the largest of the three; item order follows the base unless exactly one side reordered it; new ids from both sides are kept, ours first. Conflicts stay local: a scalar or list changed two ways, delete against edit, one new id filed with different content, both sides reordering differently (including independent swaps), and a merged result that breaks the index (a shared filing key, ids differing only in case, a dependency cycle, a dangling dependency, or discovered_from). Unreadable input falls back to the s191 text merge and is forced to a conflict if that merge came back clean. Verified on current main: tests/test_merge_fields.py and tests/test_merge_index.py; full discover 1386 tests OK (1 skipped); git diff --check clean.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** an outside-worktree store, a second driver, replacing s191's next_id policy, silently merging conflicting lists or queue reorders, or authorizing agents to hand-edit tracking JSON.

## Why

U8 revised its request after recognizing s191 and s185. Some nonoverlapping edits already merge as text, but the uncovered acceptance case is an index change whose textual hunks overlap despite independent item/field identities. The owner chose conservative list and ordering conflict handling.

## Files

The index merge driver introduced by s191, its registration/help documentation, integrity helpers, real-Git merge tests, and CHANGELOG.md.

## Failing tests

- Real branches with independent existing-item edits merge both, even when a normal text merge would overlap their hunks. Different scalar fields of one base item combine; identical changes coalesce.
- Incompatible changes to one scalar conflict at that field, leaving other independent fields merged. Different replacements/appends to the same list remain conflicts; unchanged-versus-changed lists take the changed side.
- Distinct new IDs from both sides survive with deterministic ordering. Same newly allocated ID with unequal content is a collision, even if its title happens to match.
- Delete-versus-edit conflicts; delete-versus-unchanged removes the item. Incompatible reorders of shared IDs conflict, while a reorder on only one side is retained.
- Different IDs with one nonempty filing key conflict and identify both IDs. next_id behavior remains s191's tested maximum rule.
- Test status-folder moves alongside an independent note/metadata change using actual CLI-produced branch state; after a resolved merge and render, integrity and freshness pass. Malformed/unsupported input leaves a visible conflict, never a false successful merge.

## Implement

Use the same driver and three-way base/ours/theirs inputs as s191. Match items by ID, recursively merge object fields, and treat arrays and prose strings as atomic values. A value unchanged on one side accepts the other's change; equal changes coalesce; divergent changes conflict locally. Apply this rule to nested fields and top-level prose/pass objects too.

When both sides add different IDs, retain both. Preserve base/shared item order unless exactly one side reorders it; concurrent identical reorders coalesce and incompatible ones conflict. For additions within the same gap, keep ours in order followed by theirs in order. Match IDs case-sensitively and validate case-collision rules before declaring success.

Treat unequal independently added records under the same ID as a collision, rather than fabricating one composite item. Validate nonempty key uniqueness and graph/reference/schema integrity before clean success. Preserve s191's next_id resolution. Conflicts must return nonzero with markers identifying the smallest conflicting field/order block; invalid input falls back to a visible ordinary conflict. Do not repair slice-file Git conflicts or move files behind Git's back.

Output clean merges with canonical serialization and re-render after merge through the CLI. Document that true conflicts still require an owner resolution; the driver only removes independent-field conflicts. Keep Git history-writing unreachable from slicer's runtime allowlist.
